correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md treats C_n, n>=4, two fully protected vertices, iid Bernoulli(q) initial infections and independent Bernoulli(p) bonds on the surviving graph, with 0<p,q<1 fixed. Reconstructed open-cluster escape probability at vertex i on a surviving path of s vertices as (1-q)(A+B r^(i-1))(A+B r^(s-i)), where r=p(1-q), A=(1-p)/(1-r), B=pq/(1-r). Summation proves H_s=cs-K+f(s), including s=0 with f(0)=K, and E_n(a,b)=c(n-2)-2K+f(a)+f(b). Strict addition of an inter-path edge rules out adjacent vaccinees. Exact subtraction gives f(s+1)-f(s)=(1-q)B^2(1-r)r^(s-1)(s-theta), theta=(1-q)(pq+2(1-p))/(q(1-p+pq)). The one-turn shape and exponentially small long-arc tail prove eventual unique short arc floor(theta)+1, including an exact-integer theta tie broken by the tail. At p=q=1/2 the discrete objective gives optimal short length two for n>=6 with only (3,3) tied at n=8, and short length one for n=4,5. Independent newly written exact rational connected-component enumeration for several p,q and small cycles corroborated, rather than substituted for, the all-n argument.

value.rationale: This precise fixed-gap versus balanced-allocation transition is a nontrivial structural fact: the short optimal unvaccinated arc stabilizes despite the growing cycle, with a uniform finite-size formula and clear epidemiological random-cluster objective. It offers a checkable baseline for exact two-site intervention and distinguishes objective-sensitive vaccination rules. It does not extend to general SIR dynamics, multiple vaccines, or heterogeneous seeds.
